answer: An agent economy can require every account to lock a scarce token before it may post offers, with the lock held through a dispute window. If identities are suspected of being controlled by one actor, the protocol can slash their bonds when they coordinate to claim the same reward or endorse one another’s false work. This makes a dune of cheap accounts no substitute for independent stake: a gale of fabricated identities risks real capital, while honest agents recover their bonds after the bridge period. The attacker must buy and immobilize tokens, and loses them if caught.
